text:
A: Hey! Right, I told the last fella he was my last call, so I'm officially wrong. I'm Jago.
B: Claire. I did exactly the same thing, so don't worry. Hello.
A: [laughs] Good, we're both useless. I'm in Truro. You're...?
B: Faversham, in Kent. That's a Bait poster behind you, isn't it?
A: Oh, mate, you've seen Bait? Nobody's seen Bait!
B: I saw it at a little cinema in Margate. Everyone came out looking a bit shell-shocked. I loved it. The scratchy film, the dubbed sound.
A: Yes! That's exactly it. Mark Jenkin's sort of my hero, to be honest. He hand-processes the film himself. I'm doing a film degree, final year, and I'm making a documentary about gig rowing clubs, and I keep trying to steal a bit of that look, kind of grainy, the sea and the faces.
B: Ah, you're the release forms man.
A: [laughs] Tereza really has been busy. They're signed! Most of them.
B: "Most of them" is what my business partner hears from me every week. I'm in interior design, I do the ideas, she does the paperwork.
A: See, that's the dream setup, isn't it? I'm like that on group projects. Someone else does the spreadsheet and I sort of front the pitch.
B: Hm. Does the someone else enjoy that?
A: Erm. [laughs] Probably not, if I'm honest. I bring the biscuits.
B: That's what I tell myself too. So is the film actually any good?
A: Oh, straight in. Erm... I think so? I've sent it to a couple of festivals. Some of the interviews are proper special, there's an old boy who rowed out to the Scillies. But some days I watch the rough cut and think, God, I've told everyone this is brilliant and it's just some blokes in a boat, do you know what I mean?
B: That's a better answer than "it's amazing", honestly. Everyone who makes anything thinks that. I've got half a dozen paintings in my spare room I won't finish for exactly that reason.
A: So finish them! Then we're both terrified together.
B: Maybe. What happens after you graduate?
A: Bristol, hopefully, runner or junior editor at a production house. And then Japan. It's basically booked.
B: Basically booked meaning you've looked at flights at two in the morning.
A: [laughs] Who told you?
B: I want to do Japan on my own, once my daughter's older. Same level of booked.
A: Mate, we should start a club. Have you done Lisbon? That's my favourite city in the world.
B: Lisbon's mine too. Much better than Porto, I've been arguing about it all evening.
A: Oh, no contest. Lisbon's scruffier, it's got more going on. Did you go up to the castle, the one with the—
